coverage.scope: release-critical policy, identity, redaction, data-ownership, merge-integrity, and quarantine runtime modules

gates.requirement: Focused seeded-defect detection for gates, merge, selection, quarantine, and redaction
Frozen pre-release package, action, result, and PR-report contracts
Deep tarball inspection and clean npm/pnpm exact-artifact consumers
Required hosted hardening lane and aggregate enforcement

adversarialScenarios.requirement: Clean package installation and initialization outside the monorepo
Repeated initialization is non-destructive and duplicate-free
Existing application configuration is retained during adoption
Invalid configuration is rejected before application execution
Role-authenticated workers cannot mutate unintended shared state
The same seed reproduces logical values across worker dimensions
Concurrent runs, projects, repetitions, attempts, and shards do not collide
Worker failure or restart does not leak stale authentication or test data
Cleanup cannot delete resources owned by another run
API cancellation and deadlines terminate pending work
Non-idempotent requests are not silently replayed
Feature-flag and network overrides are restored or isolated
Browser clock control does not claim to change backend time
Upload and download paths cannot escape owned temporary directories
Readiness timeout reports the real error and stops owned processes
Windows process and path handling executes on an actual Windows runner
A missing Git baseline selects full coverage
Unknown or shared-code changes conservatively broaden selection
New tests remain selected without historical results
An empty whole-suite selection fails unless explicitly justified
All expected shards merge once without losing retry attempts
Missing, duplicate, incompatible, or corrupted shards fail integrity
Reporter crash or incomplete finalization cannot produce green
Retry recovery is classified as flaky rather than clean success
Retries do not inflate the historical execution denominator
Zero or insufficient history is represented honestly
Eligible failed historical runs remain included
Incompatible consumers, environments, and revisions are not compared
Duplicate history import is idempotent and conflicts fail
Quarantine without an owner or bounded expiry is invalid
Expired quarantine is surfaced and fails the default policy gate
A quarantined failing test still produces failure
Quarantined coverage cannot disappear from release execution
Repeat-until-failure preserves the first failure and respects budgets
Meaningfully distinct failures are not collapsed by fingerprinting
Console, transport, and HTTP failures remain distinguishable
Hostile HTML, XML, Markdown, and script payloads are safely represented
Seeded canary secrets are absent from publishable text evidence
Untrusted archive paths and oversized artifacts are rejected
Missing comment permission does not erase upstream test failure
Fork PR reporting never executes PR-controlled code with write credentials
Stale workflow completion cannot overwrite a newer PR result
Failed, canceled, or missing matrix jobs cannot pass the aggregate gate
Artifact upload failure preserves original test and evidence failures
Both consumers execute through packed and published package interfaces
Published CLI templates contain required runtime and template assets
A tagged action works without building provider source
Partial package publication has a tested truthful recovery path
Breaking public contracts require the declared semantic-version policy
Serial and parallel benchmarks use equivalent test inventories

statusSemantics.PASS: Verified by retained hosted or exact-source evidence already recorded in the repository.
statusSemantics.IMPLEMENTED: Automated implementation and regression evidence exist but the new Phase 10 source revision still requires hosted acceptance.
statusSemantics.PARTIAL: Some required behavior is verified, but a named portion remains incomplete.
statusSemantics.NOT_RUN: Requires a later release or benchmark phase and is not represented as complete.
